quest.title: As Though Caught in a Dream
quest.description: You receive a long-awaited letter from Yae Miko...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: First Night
chapter.title: As Though Caught in a Dream

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Kichiboushi and the others are young, so their speaking ability is limited... I miss the days when the bake-danuki could run circles around the humans.

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Hold on, how were you able to understand them from the start? Does that mean the Bake-Danuki Meal from last time is still working...? Hah, take that, sneaky kitsune!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Speaking of... *sniff, sniff* That kitsune is gone, yes? Good. I have a request, young one. Come closer...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: You must protect the cubs from that sneaky kitsune at all costs!!!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The Lady Guuji is very... imaginative. There's no telling how the festival will end up in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She can be a handful...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I wouldn't go that far. Though outlandish at times, her ideas usually contain strokes of genius that can be quite practical in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Besides, with you and Ayaka involved in the event, trust that I will intervene if things get out of hand. You need not worry.

dialogues.speaker: Takeshi
dialogues.text: #Ah, welcome, honored {NICKNAME}. Guuji Yae told me about your visit. Please, come in.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, that was a lot easier than last time...

dialogues.speaker: Takeshi
dialogues.text: Ahem... The Almighty Shogun is also inside. It's best not to keep her waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Hmm, we need to fine tune some things if we want to take home that award... Should we add a few more mechanisms?

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Anything for Boss Thoma!

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Boss Thoma is the best!

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: Great idea, Boss Thoma!

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: Boss Thoma is best!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...Now, now, there's no need to be so stubborn about this. I'll adjust the budget here, and we'll definitely turn a profit.

dialogues.speaker: Raiden Shogun
dialogues.text: No. We must confirm the official representative before discussing details. There is an order to this that must be followed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: From the way she's talking... This must be the Shogun, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's her alright.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, little one. It's about time. Come, I have a contract for you to sign.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! We're not just gonna sign a random contract out of the blue!

choices.text: Also, if it's one of your contracts...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hardly, hardly... Well, "labor" is a part of it, but you will be compensated...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hah, so it IS as bad as Paimon thought...

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: #I see, so {F#s}he's the representative you selected... {M#He}{F#She} would indeed be the perfect candidate for the Mikawa Flower Festival.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Mikawa Flower Festival?

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: When the youkai still roamed the land, they celebrated an event known as the "Mikawa Flower Festival." It was an occasion for drink, laughter, and merriment.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: We hosted a version of it during the Test of Courage. Unfortunately, due to time constraints, we weren't able to put on a large celebration.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: So, I got to thinking, why not have another go? This time, with a Mikawa Flower Festival for youkai and humans alike.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: One that combines human ingenuity with youkai arts to offer the most innovative and thrilling entertainment of our time.... open to all humans and youkai throughout the land.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Entertainment, huh... Wait, kind of like Akitsu Yuugei and Akitsu Haneasobi? Those games were really fun!

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: For an important event like this, an official representative is required to preside over the festivities. In the past, the role was usually given to the Guuji, or an individual from the Yashiro Commission. But this time...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Neither myself nor the Kamisato family can assume the position, given we represent one side or the other — the youkai or the humans.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But, aren't I human, too?

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: Human you may be, but you posses a deep connection with the youkai, and you do not hail from this land. That makes you a more neutral option.

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: Moreover, you took part in the previous festival during the Test of Courage. In my estimation, there is no better candidate for the role.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Plus, your name has the potential to attract an even greater showing... So, are you going to sign this thing, or what?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, you've got a point... Then, let's go ahead and... Wait! Paimon almost fell into her trap!

choices.text: I don't work as a festival ambassador for free.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Come now, this is for an important occasion, is it not? Even I've chosen to throw profit to the wind. Surely a... selfless hero like yourself wouldn't turn your back on a good cause?

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: According to the proposal, the proceeds will be distributed as follows — forty percent to Yae Publishing House and ten percent to the festival representative.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, no fair!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I want thirty percent.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Now, ten percent might not sound like much, but Yae Publishing House is going to great lengths for this occasion, both in time and personnel. All you need to do is show your face.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...You say that now, and then you're going to put me to work once I agree.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hah, getting smart, aren't you, little one? In that case, I'll throw in another ten percent from the other half of the proceeds.

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: No. The other half is going to the Shogunate — that is not up for negotiation. But, I am rather curious about the supposed "great lengths" you mentioned...

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: Unless I am mistaken, most of the personnel and supplies are to be provided by the Shogunate. In that sense, forty percent seems rather high for your establishment, does it not?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That Ei... When did she reprogram you to argue back like this?

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: #Proceeds should be distributed according to contribution. Besides, from the very beginning, you planned to allocate an additional ten percent of your share to {NICKNAME}, did you not?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so earlier... you were just trying to shortchange us!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: *sigh* What's the fun in bargaining if you open up with your best offer right off the bat?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Paimon doesn't see the fun at all, but twenty percent is... acceptable.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright, so what do I have to do as the representative?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Once the representative is confirmed, the rest of the conversation goes quite smoothly.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Games have always been a central part of the festival, and both Akitsu Haneasobi and Akitsu Yuugei were extremely popular.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: So, the plan is to host an event where the attendees have forty-eight hours to create a game of their own. We'll have new and exciting entertainment in no time!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh! Everyone loves fun games! You won't have to worry about attracting humans and youkai to the event!

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: That is the general plan. I'll leave you to iron out the finer details and contact the participants.

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: This is a critical time for the Shogunate's new development plans, and the survey team is returning momentarily, so I must turn my attention to them.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Got it, got it. We'll see you later, then.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Where to now?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hmm... Chinju Forest. Let's pay a visit to our old friend, Ioroi.

choices.text: How much are you willing to offer?
How can I be sure I'm not signing myself up for slave labor or something?

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Eek! The smell of humans... Nothing to see here, just a statue... Huh? Wait, why do I smell kitsune...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Remember us, Ioroi?

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Ah! It's you youngsters... And... YOU! Hmph, the nasty kitsune who turned Chinju Forest into the playground for her Test of Courage!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Chinju Forest is supposed to be Ioroi's territory, right? No wonder he's so mad...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Exactly! How could you hold a Test of Courage without inviting me!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhhhhh, so THAT's what he's angry about!

choices.text: But, um, sealed away like this...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: ...*ahem* Anyway, what brings you all here? Something to discuss?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Okay, so he avoided the question completely...)

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, I actually came to apologize about the Test of Courage.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It was my mistake not to invite more youkai to the ceremony. So, for this Mikawa Flower Festival, I knew I had to extend a personal invitation to the bake-danuki.

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Huh? The Mikawa Flower Festival?

response.speaker: Shousei & Gyoubu Koban
response.text: Yes!!! The Mikawa Flower Festival!!!

response.speaker: Shousei & Gyoubu Koban
response.text: Yes!!! The Mikawa Flower Festival!!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Kichiboushi, Shousei, Gyoubu Koban... Where did you come from!?

choices.text: (And why can we understand them all of a sudden...)

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Hmph! Never trust an apology from a kitsune! Or an invitation, for that matter! It's just a silly festival... So what if there's delicious food!? Or fun games!?

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Yum yum!

response.speaker: "Shousei"
response.text: Fun fun!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: That's enough, you two! Don't fall for the kitsune's cheap tricks! Such hopeless innocent cubs...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: What a shame... I was hoping to take you all to the festival, but it would seem Ioroi disapproves.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I suppose it makes sense... Poor Ioroi, stuck in this statue all alone while the rest of you got to have fun. How sad that would be...

response.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
response.text: Poor Ioroi!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: E—Excuse you! I am Ioroi, the Kakushigami of the bake-danuki! I'm just... um... Ah, yes! Just worried the cubs will get distracted and stray from the tanuki path...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ah, I should also mention, I was hoping the bake-danuki could help the humans take their games to the next level, talented as you are in the art of transformation.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In Inazuma, only the bake-danuki can hope to match the kitsune in that area.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Match!? The kitsune could never rival the transformative gifts of the bake-danuki!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...Ah, well, I was thinking of using the bake-danuki as the symbol of the event in promotions and such. But, alas, it would seem you don't like that idea, Ioroi.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: No matter — I shall simply seek the help of the kitsune. When the time comes, all of Inazuma will know the kitsune stepped in to accomplish what the bake-danuki could not...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: W—Wait!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Heh.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What an obvious strategy...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It worked, didn't it?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Ahem... My dear cubs, transforming into things that already exist is only a small fraction of what it means to become a great bake-danuki...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: To even get a quarter of the way through your training, you must be able to turn into things of your own invention, just like when I turned into a gigantic ramen bowl that could fly...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: So, go forth and seize this opportunity, so you can advance the name of the... Ah, no, I mean, advance your training!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Not all humans are bad and scary — some are good, just like these youngsters. Go with them and transform into things you've never tried before.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Don't worry, Ioroi. The little tanuki are safe with me.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: You're the one I'm worried about...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we're here, too! We'll make sure they don't, uh... stray from the path!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Hm... I'll hold you to that! Now, Kichiboushi, Shousei, Gyoubu Koban, while you're out there, always listen to—

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Yep yep! Always listen to White Fur!

response.speaker: "Shousei"
response.text: #And {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} Yellow Fur!

response.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
response.text: And Auntie Pink—

response.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
response.text: ...*ahem* Miss Pink Fur!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Ah, I almost forgot, given their level of training, speaking to humans will be a problem. Just a moment, I'll cook up a few Bake-Danuki Meals to keep on hand.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: No need. Here, Miss Pink Fur prepared a special Kitsune Meal for you all. It will give you the ability to speak to humans.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mm!? Y—You stole our tricks, too? A—And changed the name!?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Seemingly oblivious to Ioroi's loud sounds of protest, Miko prepares a completely non-suspicious feast...

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Mm! Yum yum!

response.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
response.text: Nom nom! Mmm!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: *sigh*... Is it really that much better than mine...?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Splendid! That should make our lives easier. Now, we can head into the city and start forming the teams.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Teams?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Well, we need more than bake-danuki power to design these games... Hmm, two humans per team should suffice, I'd say.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Now, I need to discuss the layout of the venue with the Yashiro Commission. I'll leave the team recruitment to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on, you're not taking part, Miko? You're really gonna sit out on the fun? You, of all people...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, making games is nowhere near as fun as playing them. Besides, working through the night certainly isn't my idea of a good time.

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Making games?

response.speaker: "Shousei"
response.text: Working?

response.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
response.text: Through the night?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...Anyway, this time, I'm going to wait for the fun to come to me. See you later, little ones.

choices.text: Guess I need to earn that extra ten percent...
(Is it because of the Kitsune Meal? On second thought, better not to ask.)

talks.objective: Make your way into Inazuma City

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Eek! A city!

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: So many houses! So many humans!

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Gotta farm beans! White Fur, Yellow Fur, how do we farm beans?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Form teams not "farm beans"! Uh... It's kind of hard to explain...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's like, finding people with similar interests.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right! People with the same taste. Y'know, into the same thing. It's easier to come up with a game that way.

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Taste the same... Got it!

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: Easy peasy! White Fur, dumb.

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Farm beans that taste the same!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, wait! That's not... And, they're gone. In different directions, too! *sigh* Let's go after them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Gyoubu Koban? What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Spying on great youkai! Great youkai whisper about something with humans!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...A great youkai?
...So, what do you think? Are you interested in our proposal?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Hmm, the idea has a lot of promise, but I'm afraid there are no natural hot springs on Watatsumi island. And, the cost of heating them artificially is a bit too—
One second. I believe someone's listening... Hello over there — you're more than welcome to join, but a face-to-face conversation is more appropriate, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Eek! Great youkai found us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: I—It's just us!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: There's no need to be nervous, you two. It's not like I think you're corporate spies.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: As for you... It's been a while since I've met one of your kind. What's your name? Is Ioroi doing well?

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Eek...!

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... This is Gyoubu Koban. It's his first time visiting a city, so he's a bit shy around strangers.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: So, still sealed in that statue, then? I suppose it can't be helped...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Nice to meet you, Gyoubu Koban. My name is Yumemizuki Mizuki. I'm a yumekui-baku. We're youkai, just like you.

response.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
response.text: Great youkai is... surprisingly friendly?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Ah, looks like he was scared that, as a "great youkai," you were going to do something terrible to him for interrupting our secret meeting.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, it was actually a secret meeting...?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Not exactly, no. We were discussing the potential of opening a new branch of the Aisa Bathhouse on Watatsumi Island.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Aisa Bathhouse is expanding to Watatsumi Island?

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: Well, tourism is one of the areas we're hoping to expand. We've been discussing the possibility with Miss Mizuki for quite some time.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Still, given the lack of natural springs on Watatsumi island, we're looking at high operating costs. And, if it's not different enough from the main branch, I worry about its ability to draw in customers.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: All valid points. We do need to differentiate the brand. We could place a greater emphasis on physiotherapy...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Or add some popular activities, such as carefully designed "games"...

response.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
response.text: ...Games!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Games? In a bathhouse?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Of course! Games are often used in psychological treatment to put patients at ease.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Anyway, the topic of games really seemed to pique your interest... Is there something going on?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ahem, allow me to explain...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You briefly explain the situation to everyone...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I see... A new kind of Mikawa Flower Festival. Miss "Fried Tofu With All the Frills" is as ingenious as ever.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Miko, huh... I knew I smelled scheming in the air...

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: Oh, uh... That lady again? W—Well, there's a lot of work to do on Watatsumi Island. So, we probably don't have time for something like that... right, Your Excellency?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Hmm... I do think there's potential in turning Watatsumi Island into a tourist destination.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: We could use the festival as a proof of concept and establish a partnership with Miss Mizuki. If people are drawn to our game, that would mean a lot of positive publicity, which would benefit us in the long term.

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: Ah... B—But, aren't Aisa Bathhouse and Yae Publishing House business rivals?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Rivalries aside, I have no qualm using Yae Publishing House's resources to our advantage.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Besides, if I remember correctly, you have a connection to Yae Publishing House as well, don't you, General Gorou? You work on the That's Life column?

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: Oh, well... Yes, I do...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...If our venture is to focus on games, then as future business partners, I'm sure you would appreciate an opportunity to see what I can do.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Hehe, an astute observation, Miss Mizuki. Well, shall we? Getting down to business is often the quickest way to bring people together, after all.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...Agreed! Then, why don't we discuss some of the finer details before the festival begins?

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: Oh, but... Um... *sigh*... Alright... Then, I guess I should—

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Actually, Gorou, I was hoping you might attend to the business on Watatsumi Island in the meantime. Just as you said, there is quite a bit to be done...

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: Huh...?

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: ...Of course!

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: In addition, I'd like you to encourage the people of Watatsumi Island to attend the festival. It's a celebration for humans and youkai alike...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: ...So, that includes our people as well. This should be an occasion that brings people together.

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: ...Understood! Leave it to me, Your Excellency.

choices.text: She's giving you a way to avoid Miko.

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: White Fur! Yellow Fur! Over here! Kichiboushi found big, sleepy tanuki!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hate to break it to you Kichiboushi, but...

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Hey... I'm a mujina, not a tanuki!

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: ...Ohhh, mujina youkai that can turn into tanuki?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: No, wait... I'm not a mujina or a tanuki. I'm Sayu!

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Tanuki... Mujina... Sayu... So many transformations! Sayu is youkai?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She's a ninja, not a youkai.

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: I don't transform at all! I've been a human this whole time! Who is this guy, anyway? Popping up out of nowhere right when I found a spot to sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ehehe... Sorry, this is probably the first time Kichiboushi has ever seen a ninja...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Ah, the Big Tanuki and the Great Mujina Youkai are facing off! The rumors around Hanamizaka were true!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Not this again... It's just Sayu!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh... Haha, no youkai, huh. My bad, Sayu. I rushed over here as soon as I heard the rumors. Guess I got a bit carried away...

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: *whimper*... And there goes my nap...

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Hahaha, silly humans. Much to learn.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Whoa, hold on... Is this guy... a real youkai!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: His name is Kichiboushi.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Well, hello there, Kichiboushi!

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Mm! This human... really really warm!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Uh... warm?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Warm... personality-wise, I'm guessing?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, hahaha... Well, what brings you to Inazuma City, Kichiboushi? We don't often get bake-danuki around these parts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Boy, where do we begin...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You briefly explain the situation to Yoimiya.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Ahhh, I see. You're recruiting people to develop games for the Mikawa Flower Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You interested?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Well, duh! C'mon, Sayu! Let's do it together!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: ...Ugh! Right when I was trying to run...

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: About that... um... I'm pretty busy... uh... practicing ninjutsu and such...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, I heard the bake-danuki are great at ninjutsu! Rumors has it, with a single thought, they can grow taller than a house! Is that true, Kichiboushi?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Taller than a house? I've never heard of a ninjutsu like that...

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: It's not ninjutsu, it's bake-danuki art! We don't grow taller than house!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: S—See...? I knew it wouldn't be that easy...

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: We grow taller than mountain!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: EH!?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Sayu...?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: S—Sorry... Just thinking about something sensei always said: "You can't just focus on drills, Sayu. You need to push the limits of what you know about ninjutsu."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, this is as good an opportunity as any.

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: I... I guess...

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Farm beans, success?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: A—Alright, let's go discuss this ninjutsu... Ah, no. This bake-danuki art of transformation! The one you're going to use for the festival!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Yes! I've always wanted to go to a festival with you, Sayu! Let's go to my place to brainstorm! We can even set off some fireworks when we're done!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Uh... I'll pass on the fireworks. They're terrible for my sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: ...Wait, you're saying he's not one of Ushi's friends?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Whoa, pump the brakes... I thought he was your friend.

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: Hehe, long-horned oni and short-horned oni!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: He... He talks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shousei! There you are!

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: White Fur! Yellow Fur! Shousei found White Fur and Yellow Fur number two. Both great youkai! Both like to play!

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Great youkai... So, he thinks I'm an oni, too?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Listen, I was just playin' some Genius Invokation with my good bro Thoma during his time off...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: And then, out of the blue, this... Shousei appeared right in the middle of our match.

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: Shousei loves to play! Long-horned and short-horned Oni also love to play! We taste the same, hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: We what now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can explain...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You briefly explain the situation to Itto and Thoma...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Oho! The Mikawa Flower Festival! Shoulda opened with that, compadre!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Man, the Arataki Gang really hard-carried the last one. We'll turn this one into somethin' special, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hitotsume Kozou and the others did all the work, Bull-chucker. You're really lumping them in with your gang?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I—It's called doing them a favor... Besides, they look up to me. I'm like a cool older brother...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Hitotsume Kozou and his friends did come up with the Akitsu Yuugei game during the last festival. There's no reason not to invite them this time!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Woo, the crew's gettin' back together! I'll round 'em up, hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: ...Technically, I'm on vacation, but I'm happy to assist the Yashiro Commission with the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: That's what I like to hear! Alright, let's round up those three little fellas and start workin' on the Almighty Arataki Great and Glorious Akitsu Yuugei Game...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Not so fast.

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: ...Hornless oni?

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: We have an advertising job to finish, remember, Boss?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Huh?? We... We do!?

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Re-shoots, follow-up work... There's still a mountain of things to do.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Oh, well... uh...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: *ahem* Look at Thoma here, kind enough to help with the festival even during his vacation. I would think the Boss of the Arataki Gang would show even more dedication to his work, but y'know, that's just me...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Uhh... Umm...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Hah... Looks like your time is spoken for, my friend.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Wrap up what you need to do, and we can finish our match at the festival. Best of both worlds!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Alright! Those errands are a piece of cake. I'll be back in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Oh, but first, I should introduce you to Kozou and the others. Then, you can head to the festival... without me.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: #Then, let's get a move on! No use standing here talking about it — go make those introductions. We have stuff to do... Sorry, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. I'm sure we'll see you later.

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: Hornless oni, so scary...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm, I think I'm good. I don't need to make a call right away.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, you don't want to judge an unfinished product? Well, that does make sense...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: There are fun things to do at some of the stalls nearby. You can check them out while the contestants work on their games.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You spend some time perusing the stalls and play-testing "Bunshin Phantasm," "Akitsu Harpastum," and "A Little Fox's Daydream."\nSoon, night falls.

dialogues.speaker: Hirotatsu
dialogues.text: Miss Kamisato, this is the list of the stage materials for your review...

dialogues.speaker: Madarame Hyakubei
dialogues.text: Miss Kamisato, I have your schedule for tomorrow...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Hmm... The list looks fine. As for the schedule, let's move the meeting with the Tenryou Commission up a little. They're in charge of festival security, so that should take precedence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, she looks super busy... Should we come back later?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: #Hm? Oh... {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: ...Oh, no. You're fine. You caught me just as I was finishing up, actually.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Lady Guuji said you're the official festival representative, and you've been busy recruiting participants... So, I should do my part too, right?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: For large events like the Test of Courage, Brother usually does most of the organizing. But this time, I wanted to take some work off his back.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That should be a big help!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I hope so!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, speaking of the recruitment, we found a bunch of people! We should be good to go!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Oh, already? That was fast... I wasn't sure we would find enough participants. I thought I might have to sign up myself...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Oh, don't worry about it. I can only focus on so many things, anyway. If we have enough people, I should stick to organizing.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I suppose I'm a little sad about not taking part... But, I'm looking forward to the festival all the same.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: When the time comes, perhaps we could check it out tog—

response.speaker: Hirano
response.text: Miss Kamisato! Another letter from the Kanjou Commission!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Ah! Coming! ...Sorry, duty calls. We'll have to talk about our plans another time.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: My brother's the one overseeing the teams. I believe he's in the courtyard with Lady Guuji. You can go in when you're ready.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks, Ayaka! See you later!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: See you later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Ayaka's really working hard... Guess we should follow suit. You're the festival representative, and that makes Paimon the representative of the representative. So, in other words, let's do this!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ah, it's about time... I could hear you talking outside.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I apologize for not greeting you upon arrival. The Lady Guuji and I were discussing something urgent.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, don't worry about it! We were talking to Ayaka, anyway.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: #Heh, now that young lady is one enthusiastic volunteer, especially when she heard about your involvement, {NICKNAME}. Solved our personnel problem in one fell swoop...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, you took the opportunity to order her around as well?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hardly... It was entirely her decision. Besides, you really think I could order her around with her big brother standing right there?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I do hope she gets what she wants out of the event... Now, I see the bake-danuki are no longer with you. I assume that means the teams are set?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yep. Here's the situation...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You explain what happened to Ayato...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Heh... Long-horned oni and short-horned oni. Those are some interesting names.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I was hoping Thoma would use the festival as an excuse to relax, but it would seem he refuses to remain idle.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: He even signed up as a participant... Well, here's to hoping the game development is enjoyable, at the very least.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: #...Ah, Mizuki signed up, too? Along with the "Sole of the Deep"? Now, this is getting interesting... I knew it was a good idea to put you in charge of recruitment, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They're planning to use your festival to promote Aisa Bathhouse!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, is that so? Then, perhaps I should up the ante...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, Ayato... Is everything set on your end, then?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Yes. The Yashiro Commission will be in contact with each team and arrange for lodging, food, equipment, and travel.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: We will also determine the overall theme for the games, which will be announced forty-eight hours before the opening of the festival.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes, yes, that's all well and good. I just have one small adjustment...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, why so anxious? I'm just trying to keep things exciting! When we're ready to announce the theme, come to the festival grounds at the foot of Mt. Yougou. We'll see you there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Time really flew by today! It's so late already...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The game booths were cool, but the food was even better! There were vendors selling Dango Milk, Tricolor Dango, Rice Cake Soup, you name it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Of course you care about the food the most...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, Paimon saved a skewer just for you! Here, before it gets cold!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's not something you just didn't finish, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: N—No! Of course not! If you don't want it, Paimon will eat it herself!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (You enjoy the soft and chewy texture of the snack. With the excitement of the festival all around you, it almost tastes sweeter than usual.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tastes great, right? Which means... We should come back for more tomorrow!

choices.text: So that's why you saved one for me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe... Wait! Do you see that up ahead? What's someone doing out this late...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, their clothes look kinda weird... Oh, could they be one of those costumed actors Miko mentioned?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Hello there! Are you also here for the festival?
...Hyah!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon! Watch out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Waaaah!!!

choices.text: You've run out Mora to buy it yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: ...Though the festival has yet to begin, the game development process is sure to attract a crowd.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: It is the Tenryou Commission's responsibility to maintain security and order throughout the entirety of the proceedings. So, remain vigilant. Understood?

dialogues.speaker: Haruto
dialogues.text: Yes, Ma'am!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Sara!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You guys are here early! There's still three whole days until the festival starts...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Correction — there's a little over forty-eight hours. Besides, many patrons are already here to observe the development process. Festival security starts now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but what about the Statue of the, uh... Almighty... Narukami, uh... Ogo— Eh, you know the one. Won't you miss out on it again?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Want us to buy one for you?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: ...Heh, no need. All Statues of Her Excellency, the Almighty Narukami Ogosho, God of Thunder being sold at this event are an old model.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: And as it turns out... I already own five of said model at home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, okay... Well, that's definitely more than enough...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Yes, I only own five Statues of Her Excellency at any given time. That is my maximum.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Any more, and I'm afraid I would not be able to afford them the proper care.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, THAT'S the reason?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: ...Personal matters aside, I heard you are the representative for this event. You should proceed to the stage and speak with the Lady Guuji.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right... Looks like we're running out of time. Let's go, then! See you later, Sara.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Inoue
dialogues.text: ...Ma'am! We have a message from Commission headquarters. They need you to return as soon as possible!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Headquarters...? Now, of all times? Alright, keep watch in my absence. I won't be long.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here! Now, we can get the ball rolling...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are we late?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Right on time, I'd say. I was just about to announce the theme for the games.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uhh, what's that thing behind you...?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh, this? Just a little something to spice things up.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: So... stay tuned!

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Hmm... We should be getting close, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: So sleepy... Can't wait any more...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: A theme decided by Miko and the Yashiro Commission... What's it gonna be...?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: One thing we all share... is our capacity to dream.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Outlandish fantasies of the mind, nostalgic memories of the past, or telling reflections of our inner selves...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: In a similar sense, games also blur the lines between fantasy and reality. Just like our dreams, the bounds of possibility are as limitless as our imagination.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...With that in mind, your task is to create a game within the next forty-eight hours centered around the theme of "dreams." The genre and style are completely up to you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... Nothing too crazy so far...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: And, to provide some additional motivation...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The winning team will be awarded the Tanuki Game Award!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: As well as a generous sum of Mora... AND a sponsorship from Yae Publishing House to fully develop the game and promote it throughout all Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Mm!?

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: A—All Inazuma!?

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Thump thump... *squeal*!?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: In the interest of fairness, the evaluation committee will decide the winner based on attendee feedback as well as the opinion of our festival representative.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Now, with that out of the way, let the game development begin! The forty-eight hour countdown... begins now.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Although Miko's sudden announcement leaves people reeling, the teams quickly get to work...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hm, looks like things are going well. We've just started, and it seems like all our teams have a plan.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Plus, with the transformative powers of the bake-danuki, bringing those visions to fruition should be a lot easier.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: As the festival's most important judge and representative... You should go check on the progress, don't you think?

choices.text: I really didn't see that coming...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It all comes down to fairness, as I said. I worked with the Yashiro Commission to come up with the theme, so the judging must go to someone else.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: No need to stress, though. It's all fun and games, is it not? Just choose the one you enjoy the most.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Of course, if it's appearances you're worried about, you could always... Oh, I don't know... check in on the teams and ask about their ideas?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, and that proves that I picked the right person. Go on, then — I won't keep you.

choices.text: I plan to take this seriously, like I always do.
Me as the main judge? Really?

talks.objective: Share your play-test experience with Miko

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Alright... Let's add another elemental reaction here...

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou & Kappa
dialogues.text: Boss Thoma is the best!

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou & Kappa
dialogues.text: Boss Thoma is the best!

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Heh, that's nice of you, but it's all thanks to Akitsu Yuugei that I came up with this in the first place, and that was all you...

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Anything for Boss Thoma!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Guess this team really hit it off...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: #Oh, hi there, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like you're getting along great with Kozou and the others! Guess a "fixer" can work with just about anyone, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Haha, I have Itto to thank, actually. He introduced me to Kozou and the others after you left that day.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: We didn't get to see each other much during the Test of Courage, but they're a very friendly group of youkai...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: All I had to do was mention the Mikawa Flower Festival, and they agreed to help right away. They even showed up bright and early this morning.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That makes sense! It was their dream to host the Mikawa Flower Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: ...Yep! That's right!

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Yeah, totally! We've been dreaming about it for a long time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what are you planning for the game? It kinda sounded like you're making a sequel to Akitsu Yuugei!

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Hmm... I suppose it's a spiritual sequel of sorts? It's a combination of Akitsu Yuugei and Mondstadt's Ludi Harpastum...I call it, "Akitsu Harpastum."

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: It's pretty simple, actually. Just swing the racket to hit the balls back where they came from.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, but what does that have to do with the theme?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Haha... Good question. The Lady Guuji did say that reminiscing about "nostalgic memories" is a form of dreaming, right?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: For many years after leaving Mondstadt, the only place I could experience Ludi Harpastum was in my dreams...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Once I was old enough to go back on my own, too much had changed... My age, my mindset... Whatever it was, the Ludi Harpastum of my childhood was gone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thoma...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: So, I suppose you could say, "Akitsu Harpastum" is a childhood dream many years in the making.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Oh, and in the play-test stage, I added a few characters that often appear in fairytales and dreamscapes.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: ...Hopefully, that reinforces the theme a bit more, haha. Wanna give it a try?

response.speaker: "Shousei"
response.text: Haha! White Fur, Yellow Fur, get ready!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha, I almost forgot! You're an important figure in this event! Well, don't let us keep you. Come back any time!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I want to look around some more...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh? Well, hurry back. Don't keep me waiting for too long!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You share your play-test insights with Miko...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Mmm, fascinating... Which game are you looking forward to the most?

talks.objective: Share your play-test experience with Miko

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Look at this! You've made so much progress already!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, all credit to Kichiboushi! We just told him what we wanted, and he made the set in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: He helped with the gameplay, too... All we had was a prototype, and now it's ready for play-testing already. His skills are amazing...

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Hm! Kichiboushi, amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Very amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, um... how do we play? It doesn't seem super obvious...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The board is infused with youkai power! All you need to do is place your hand on it to enter the "dreamscape"... At least, I think that's how it works, right, Kichiboushi?

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Orange Fur, very smart!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you could say your game unifies human ingenuity with bake-danuki magic to create a scene that is completely illusory... Very creative!

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: White Fur, suddenly use many big words...

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: You sure sound official all of a sudden, Paimon... Are you trying to act like a real judge?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't mind her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm... This new style of game development deserves a name! How about "Unreal"? Ooh! Or "Unity"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell us about your game?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: You betcha!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Hey, a little acknowledgment would be nice!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Although, Sayu's the better person to ask! "Bunshin Phantasm" is her brain-child, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Bunshin Phantasm"?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Yeah! It's based on a dream I had... In the dream, I learned to make bunshin, and I made them do all my work for me.

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: With my clones around, there was no reason for that lady to come find me, so I could sleep as long as I wanted...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So even when you're asleep, you dream of getting more sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: It's just... I got so excited at the prospect that I actually woke myself up... *sigh* If only I could make bunshin in real life...

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Well, then... Even if some get caught, the others could take a nap in the meantime, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if your clones do all the work, doesn't all that fatigue transfer back to you in the end?

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Oh, well, um... When you put it that way... I don't know anymore...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: All dreams are nonsensical and complicated in their own way. But that's what makes them interesting!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Anyway, that's our game — "The Most Wonderful Bunshin Phantasm: Mujina Body Doubles to the Rescue!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's a... mujina body double?

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: That's a long story... Wanna just give it a try?

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Awesome! All you have to do is put your hand on the board and close your eyes...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Ah, right! You have other teams to check out! All good! Whenever you're ready to play, just touch the board, and you're good to go!

choices.text: Your clones might not want to work any more than you do...

talks.objective: Share your play-test experience with Miko

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Mizuki, Kokomi, and Gyoubu Koban! How are things going over here?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Not bad — we've made a lot of progress. Miss Mizuki is very experienced, and Gyoubu Koban's abilities are simply astonishing.

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Piece of cake! *click click*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Experienced, huh... That must put you at a huge advantage! Is it because you use games in your work?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Hmm, I'm not sure it gives me an advantage, per se... The games I use are for clinical purposes, not entertainment.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: But if we want that award, we need something a lot more fun. So, my experience only goes so far.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: That reminds me... The Yashiro Commission chose "dreams" as the theme of the competition. Do you think that was targeted at us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, using "dreams" to test a dream-eater... Yeah, it does sound like some kind of challenge...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: They knew we wanted to use this as an opportunity to advertise our game. But, now, it's a competition...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Which means, if we lose, our game will be completely overshadowed by the winner.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: And if we win, she gets a share of the profits as the primary investor... Miss "Fried Tofu With All the Frills" is on the top of her game.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... That's a lot of scheming...

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Mm? Screaming?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: On the other hand, if we do win first place, the prestige will help us get the word out, which should increase the popularity of the bathhouse on Watatsumi Island.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: As for Yae Publishing House's sponsorship... As long as we win the competition, we get to decide the terms.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Winner takes all, huh... I suppose it works both ways. This definitely has the Lady Guuji written all over it.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: My guess... is that she's doing all this for the entertainment factor — for fun, basically.

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Mm! Fun, fun! Gyoubu Koban likes fun!

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Heh, well said. I suppose that's the purpose of a game, after all. For now, let's focus on making our game the best it can be.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good idea! So, what kind of game are you gonna make?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: We're calling it, "A Little Fox's Daydream." Basically, you play as a fox navigating between sweet dreams and nightmares in search of delicious fried tofu.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I might know who the "little fox" is supposed to be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, looks like that fox takes some inspiration from, uh... real life...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Well, the design was Miss Mizuki's idea, but I'm completely on board. Sometimes, the only way to meet a challenge is with a challenge of your own.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Fighting fire with fire, huh...)

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: That's the definition of fun, don't you think? So, wanna give it a try?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Wonderful! Right this way...

response.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
response.text: Next time, next time! That's a promise!

talks.objective: Share your play-test experience with Miko

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think so.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh? And what are your thoughts? I'm all ears.

talks.objective: Share your play-test experience with Miko
Share your play-test experience with Miko

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we had to pick one, but honestly, all the ideas were pretty good...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: It's still early days, so there's no rush to make a decision. Plenty of novels at Yae Publishing House have opened on a high note, only to lose the plot halfway through.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: You can pick your favorite game once everyone's done with their work.

talks.objective: Share your play-test experience with Miko

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm, guess I should go back and check things out some more...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: That's the spirit! Give the games another look, and I'm sure one of them will speak to you. Go on, now.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Just think, all the kids in Inazuma might have a chance to play our game! Ah, I'm so excited! We have to win!

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Have to win!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: O—Or, we could take a more laid back approach? I mean, we shouldn't jeopardize our sleep or anything...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hm, you have a point... The most important thing is to have fun.

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Oh, and learning a ninjutsu to grow taller! *ahem* I mean, learning new ninjutsu in general, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is that it...?)
...Hyah!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So fast!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (When did this dagger get here?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hold on, I know this feeling... I've felt it several times before...!)
...Hyah!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'm in a dream!!!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}! Hey! Are you alright!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What just happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you fought that strange person and made them disappear. But then, all of a sudden, you started backing up like you were super afraid of something...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...I'm fine now, don't worry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... You nearly gave Paimon a heart attack...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I saw a dagger, but it was Tricolor Dango the whole time... So, it was all just a nightmare?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Luckily, I heard the sound of thunder in the dream. Otherwise, it probably would have taken me a lot longer to break out of the nightmare...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, what was with that thunder just now? It came out of nowhere, and it's not even raining!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So the thunder... wasn't part of the dream?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Who was that person...?)

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...Has a "Nightmare" returned to Inazuma once again?

dialogues.speaker: Asari
dialogues.text: Hey, Komura! Time to go. The stalls are closed, so let's head home for the night!

dialogues.speaker: Asari
dialogues.text: Hey! Did you hear me? No more gaming tonight. We can come back tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Asari
dialogues.text: ...Komura, Komura!

dialogues.speaker: Asari
dialogues.text: Um... Komura?
What's with the yelling? I can hear you just fine. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Asari
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Komura
dialogues.text: ...What? You're not coming? Why are you giving me that look?

dialogues.speaker: Asari
dialogues.text: Komura, weren't you...

dialogues.speaker: Asari
dialogues.text: Over there... just now?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Well? Did you get a good look at all the games?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh? Back so soon? Did you want to withhold judgment until they're done?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sayu's "Bunshin Phantasm"...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Bunshin, huh... I'm not surprised she's interested in learning that ninjutsu. I suppose I could find an opportunity to teach her...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you know how to make bunshin!?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Well, if it's conjuring a body double to sit at the shrine in my place, that's child's play. I'm sure plenty of youkai can do the same.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, but best not let Nana find out... Pretend I didn't say anything, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thoma's "Akitsu Harpastum"...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Akitsu Harpastum, huh? I'm sure that will be a nostalgic experience for many people.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm, perhaps a Mondstadt spin on an Inazuman classic will be... Dare I say, a breath of fresh air...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: What do you say we drag Ei out here so she can join in on the fun?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mizuki's "A Little Fox's Day—"

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (You quickly cut yourself off upon sensing a sharp look from Miko.)

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: What an interesting take on the theme... Tell me, did it come from Miss "Sole of the Deep" or my dear, old friend?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're not going to charge them for using your likeness, are you...?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Heh, not a bad idea. But, I'm more interested in seeing how this plays out, which means... turning a blind eye, for now.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Oh, here's an idea... Let's make the final checkpoint of this stage a ramen stand.

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Hm? Ramen stand? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Let me guess... another callback to the real-life Lady Guuji?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The Lady Guuji's decision to turn this into a competition certainly was... unexpected. But, I digress... What do you think of the award?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Is that so? Hehe, make sure to let Ayaka know you think so.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Ah, well... It was a bit last minute...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I can't believe I finished everything in time... That was close.

choices.text: Organizing a competition out of thin air...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Yeah... It was a very last-minute change of plans. We had to get a bunch of supplies ready, like the Tanuki Game Award, which took a while.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: If only I had a bit more time, I'm sure I could have made it look better...

choices.text: That must have been a lot of work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? A letter from Miko? What is she plotting this time... Well, let's open it and take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Tenshukaku? Why does she want to meet us there? Paimon has a bad feeling about this...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh, but before I forget, you should eat this Kitsune Meal first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it smells so good... Hmm... Oh, and also kind of like fried tofu, for some reason?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, that should be enough teams! Time to report back to the Yashiro Commission!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The theme for the games is being announced today, right? Who knows what Miko's got up her sleeve... Let's go check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you need to pick the "best game," huh... Well, why don't we take a look around to get a feel for things? Then, we can go talk to Miko!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright — we checked out each of the games! Wanna give any of them another go? If not, let's head back and find Miko.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What was that for!? They attacked us out of nowhere!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Something's not right about this... B—Be careful, Traveler!
